name: Orbital decompression
lead: Orbital decompression is surgery that enlarges the effective volume of the eye socket by removing orbital bone, orbital fat, or both, allowing the eye to sit further back. Its established use is in thyroid eye disease (Graves' orbitopathy), where swollen muscle and fat push the eye forward (proptosis) and can compress the optic nerve.[9][10]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way for people without thyroid disease to get deeper-set eyes by reducing protrusion, and members debate who is a candidate, which technique (fat removal or bone work) is used, and its risks.[18][21]

The clinical literature on orbital decompression concerns people with thyroid eye disease. Randomised trials and case series compare surgical approaches and report outcomes such as proptosis reduction and sight-threatening optic neuropathy.[7][8][9] No published trial located assesses the procedure for purely cosmetic deep-setting in people with normal thyroid and orbital status, and the surgery is an operation in the orbit with documented risks to vision and eye movement.[9][5]

paras: Graves' orbitopathy, also called thyroid eye disease, is an autoimmune condition in which the orbital muscles and fat swell, producing proptosis, eyelid retraction, double vision and sometimes optic nerve compression. Irish surgeon Robert Graves described the link between thyroid enlargement and eye protrusion in 1835.[10]

Guidelines emphasise stage-adapted anti-inflammatory therapy, risk-factor control including smoking cessation, and rehabilitative surgery after inflammation stabilises. Compressive optic neuropathy is treated as an emergency.[1][3][5] Orbital decompression is used both urgently for optic neuropathy and electively to reduce proptosis.[10]

Decompression removes bone from one or more orbital walls, with or without orbital fat removal, to let tissue expand. Approaches include endoscopic transnasal (reported in 1990),[12] transantral (a 1993 series of 428 patients),[13] transcaruncular,[14] and transconjunctival or transnasal endoscopic comparisons.[7] A 2006 paper described transpalpebral orbital lipectomy as an alternative.[11]
Surgery for thyroid eye disease is typically delayed until disease has been stable for at least six months unless the optic nerve is threatened.[10]

A 2025 randomised trial of 48 moderate-to-severe or sight-threatening orbits compared transconjunctival and transnasal endoscopic decompression, with effectiveness defined by postoperative proptosis or proptosis reduction.[7] A randomised trial of rehabilitative decompression in Graves' orbitopathy and another combining decompression with intraoperative muscle relaxation for esotropia have also been published.[8][9]

Reported complications in thyroid eye disease include optic neuropathy, corneal exposure, persistent double vision and raised intraocular pressure.[10] A case report describes vision loss and recurrent proptosis after an uncomplicated fat-only decompression.[6] Persistent diplopia and new strabismus are recognised outcomes in the literature, and orbital compartment syndrome is described as an ophthalmic surgical emergency.[15]
A forum reply to a thread on the topic cites a 9.3% complication rate and calls it one of the riskiest hardmaxxing procedures.[19]

Clinical studies involve patients with thyroid eye disease: randomised trials of surgical approach,[7][8][9] registered trials of customised multi-wall decompression and rim-sparing lateral wall techniques,[16][17] and case series.[13] No study was found of orbital decompression for cosmetic deep-setting of eyes in people without thyroid disease.

Threads ask how to tell if cosmetic orbital decompression is needed, who qualifies, whether it is superior to other eye surgeries, and the difference between surgeons who remove fat and those who shave bone.[18][21][22][23][24] Some repliers recommend orbital fat grafting as an alternative for people who do not have markedly protruding eyes, and others discuss a fear of botched outcomes.[19] Members also post personal accounts of surgery with a named surgeon.[20]

timeline.event: Robert Graves describes the link between thyroid enlargement and eye protrusion.[10]
Endoscopic transnasal orbital decompression is described.[12]
A series of 428 transantral decompressions for severe Graves' ophthalmopathy is reported.[13]
EUGOGO publishes updated medical management guidelines for Graves' orbitopathy.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org orbital decompression is regarded as one of the most aggressive eye hardmaxxing options, and threads compare candidacy, technique and botch risk.[18][19][21][22]

claims.claim: Orbital decompression is the way to get deep-set eyes if yours protrude.
claims.believers: Posters ask whether it is the only way to fix protruding eyes and whether it is superior to other eye surgeries.[22][23]
claims.experts: Established indications are thyroid eye disease and compressive optic neuropathy; no cosmetic-indication trials were found.[1][9]

claims.claim: Only people with genuinely bulging eyes are candidates; others should use fat grafts instead.
claims.believers: A reply states that it is for people with 'genuine bug eyes' and suggests orbital fat grafts for others.[19]
claims.experts: The literature defines proptosis thresholds in thyroid eye disease trials (for example postoperative proptosis under 18 mm as one outcome criterion), not cosmetic candidacy.[7]

claims.claim: The surgery is high-risk and can cause botched or sight-threatening outcomes.
claims.believers: Posters cite a 9.3% complication rate and a fear of blindness or asymmetry.[19]
claims.experts: Reviews and case reports describe optic neuropathy, diplopia and vision loss after decompression in thyroid eye disease.[6][10]

claims.claim: Surgeons differ on whether to remove fat or bone, and this changes results.
claims.believers: One thread notes some surgeons remove fat while others shave bone.[18]
claims.experts: Trials compare approaches in thyroid eye disease; outcomes depend on technique and disease severity.[7][13]

card.summary: Orbital bone or fat removal that lets the eye sit deeper; a thyroid-eye-disease operation with no trials for cosmetic deep-setting.
card.aka: Cosmetic orbital decompression, deep-set eye surgery
card.note: Orbital surgery with risks to vision and eye movement; evidence comes from thyroid eye disease, not cosmetic use.

quick.overview:
Orbital decompression enlarges the eye socket by removing bone, fat or both so the eye sits further back. It is an established operation for thyroid eye disease, where swollen tissue pushes the eyes forward or threatens the optic nerve.

Looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a way to get deeper-set eyes without thyroid disease and debate candidacy and technique. No published trial studies it for that cosmetic purpose.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons remove parts of orbital walls (medial, lateral, floor) and/or orbital fat via endoscopic, conjunctival or other approaches, giving swollen or prominent contents room to move backward.
quick.risks: Reported complications in thyroid eye disease include optic neuropathy, corneal exposure, persistent double vision and raised eye pressure, and vision loss after decompression has been described in case reports. Forum posters call it among the riskiest hardmaxxing procedures.
